columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Launched July 2023 as a separate app tied to TikTok; shut down November 28, 2024, with users advised to migrate playlists elsewhere.
Catalogs from Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group, and Sony Music while active.
Subscription-only model (no free tier like Spotify / YouTube Music).
Features included collaborative playlists, lyric search, personalized suggestions, offline listening, synced lyrics, and song comments/reactions shared back into TikTok.

strengths.title: Tight integration with TikTok discovery (while active)
strengths.detail: Built to make saving and streaming full songs seen on TikTok seamless, bridging short-form discovery and full-length listening.

strengths.title: Full-featured streaming experience (while active)
strengths.detail: Standard streaming features (playlists, offline, lyrics, personalization) plus social reactions back to TikTok.

weaknesses.title: Limited regional rollout and short lifespan
weaknesses.detail: Never widely launched globally; shut down after ~1.5 years, limiting adoption.

weaknesses.title: Subscription-only model
weaknesses.detail: No free tier made it harder to compete against freemium incumbents like Spotify and YouTube Music.

weaknesses.title: Strategic pivot to in-app tools, not a full streamer
weaknesses.detail: TikTok now leans into music tools inside the main app rather than competing as a standalone subscription music service.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. TikTok Music is former standalone TikTok music streaming app (2023–2024); strategy now centers on in-app music tools rather than a separate streamer. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

TikTok Music was a standalone music streaming app that combined TikTok’s discovery with a full-featured subscription music service, offering catalog streaming, playlist tools, and social song reactions before shutting down in November 2024. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and TikTok Music side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On TikTok Music you can use Audio as a first-class product job. You want a dedicated listening app, playlists, and the catalog people already pay a subscription for.

Using Kahana with TikTok Music

You can use both. TikTok Music keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep listening on TikTok Music, where the catalog and players are strongest. Put episode lists, companion notes, and Club discussion on Kahana so assigned audio is a library item, not only a For You row.
